author: Orienta
name: Find the particles in an aluminium matrix
notes:
Groups the map into chemically distinct areas and names them from your CIF library.

GOOD FOR: precipitates and inclusions a few micrometres across in an aluminium matrix.
NOT FOR: layered samples, heavily mixed microstructures, or any scan whose dominant element is not aluminium - this preset pins Al as the matrix element and will refuse those rather than measure enrichment against the wrong baseline.

This is a sensible starting point you can then correct. It is not the correct answer: expect to merge two areas that are really one particle, and to split one that is really two.

SMOOTHING is stated as 2.5 um - a physical width, not a pixel count - so it means the same analysis at any step size. Measured on the SampleB test scan (0.5 um step, 90x120 px, 8 elements) that is a 5 px box: 7 distinct areas, 0.933 of neighbouring pixel pairs in the same area, 74 connected pieces. Features thinner than the box are absorbed, so if your particles are around 2 um or smaller, lower it - 1.5 um on the same scan gave 227 pieces: more detail, and more confetti.

CANDIDATE PHASES are whatever your CIF library holds. This preset does not pin a list, because it cannot know yours - which makes it convenient and NOT reproducible: add a CIF next month and it quietly does something different. Once you know which phases you care about, save your own copy with the list pinned.
